report.source_text: A muscle biopsy from the left rectus femoris revealed histological findings reflecting active muscle fiber necrosis and regenerative changes (Fig. 2). Reactive mononuclear cell infiltration was seen surrounding necrotic and regenerating fibers. Immunostaining showed the expression of human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-ABC and deposition of membrane attack complex (MAC) on the muscle fiber membranes. Perifascicular atrophy, fibers with internal nuclei, and endomysial fibrosis were not seen. No perivascular collections of inflammatory cells were apparent. The pathological findings were suggestive of immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM), as confirmed by a neurologist specializing in muscle disease (IN).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 69-year-old woman presented with unexplained weight loss over 3 years and mild proximal muscle weakness. Labs on admission showed elevated muscle enzymes (CK 1081 IU/L, aldolase 12.7 IU/L) and inflammatory markers. EMG showed a myogenic pattern consistent with inflammatory myopathy. Muscle biopsy revealed active muscle fiber necrosis, mononuclear cell infiltration, HLA-ABC expression, and MAC deposition without perifascicular atrophy, suggesting immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy. Serology revealed positive anti-PM/Scl-75 antibody and negative other myositis-specific antibodies. Chest CT showed mild bilateral lower lung interstitial changes. The patient responded to oral prednisolone with clinical and CK improvement.
